canopy.name: Ginkgo

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal: the cotyledons stay inside the big seed; the shoot comes up with a few fan-shaped leaves that are often deeply notched into two or more lobes. Young trees are gawky, sparsely branched spires with a strong leader and a few long, widely spaced branches; the crown fills out and broadens only after several decades.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Ginkgo biloba: 20-35 m, some >40 m; specimens >1600 yr, largest estimated >3500 yr; conical crown when young, broader and irregular with age); Del Tredici (ginkgo ecology). Growth-age curve and first-seed age from horticultural records (females bear at ~20-30 yr).

canopy.source: Wild in the Tianmu and Dalou mountains of E China; the last of its line, unchanged since the dinosaurs. Fan leaves turn pure gold in one week each autumn, then drop all at once. Dioecious; wind-pollinated; fetid seeds carried by mammals. Kew POWO.

canopy.name: Tulip tree

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two narrow, oblong cotyledons, then the unmistakable square-ended, four-lobed 'tulip' leaves on a straight green stem. In full light seedlings bolt from their second year and may be 3-5.5 m tall at five years: a straight, slender, grey-green whip with a narrow conical crown. Stump sprouts grow even faster, about 1.4 m a year.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 2 (Liriodendron tulipifera: 70-90 day stratification, epigeal; 3-5.5 m at 5 yr; site index 30 m: 15.8 m at 20 yr, 27 m at 40, 32 m at 60, 37 m at 100; flowers at 15-20 yr; 30-46 m mature, to 61 m; lives 200-250, up to 300 yr; shade-intolerant).

growth.juvenile_note: Spores sprout in 10-15 days into heart-shaped prothalli on damp soil; about 3 months later the first tiny fronds unroll, simple and fan-lobed, then pinnate. A one-year plant is a loose shuttlecock of soft, lacy, pale-green twice-pinnate fronds 30-45 cm long, often on reddish stalks, from an upright crown; it dies back each autumn.
growth.source: Univ. Washington ESRM 412 propagation protocol (spores germinate in 10-15 d, sporophytes ~3 months, 45 cm plant with 7 fronds in 1 yr, spore-bearing fronds 2 yr after germination); NC State Extension; Minnesota Wildflowers; lifespan estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds sown in autumn come up the next spring or the one after. The seedling shows two cotyledons, then for several years a single small, shallowly lobed umbrella leaf on a short stalk, a little larger each year as the rhizome thickens. Only mature rhizomes send up the forked, two-leaved stalk with one nodding white flower. Leaves yellow and vanish by midsummer.
growth.source: NC State Extension (30-45 cm; flowers April-May; seedlings take several years to mature; summer dormant; deep to partial shade); Wikipedia (sterile one-leaf and fertile two-leaf shoots; colonies grow from one creeping rhizome). Germination delay, age at first flower and ramet lifespan estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds shed in early summer come up the next spring as just two small oval cotyledons for a whole season; the next year brings a single small three-lobed leaf on a long stalk. Young plants stay single leaves from a thin brown rhizome for years, then send up a stem with a whorl of three deeply cut leaves and one white, often pink-flushed flower; all top growth dies back by midsummer.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Anemonoides nemorosa: rhizomatous perennial under 30 cm of shady woods; flowers Mar-May in Britain; summer dormant by midsummer; hoverfly-pollinated; slow-spreading ancient-woodland indicator) and Shirreffs 1985 (Biological Flora, J. Ecol.) as recalled: seeds germinate the spring after shedding, several years to flowering. Rates and ages estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two oval cotyledons, then glossy dark green 3-5-lobed leaves with pale veins on a creeping purplish stem that roots along the ground and climbs with rows of tiny aerial roots, carpeting deep shade. Only shoots that reach bright light high up (after ~10+ yr) turn 'adult': bushy, rootless, with unlobed oval leaves, flowers and berries.
growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Hedera helix): 60-100% germination within ~15 days once pulp is removed; 3-5-lobed juvenile leaves with aerial roots vs unlobed adult leaves; ~30-40 yr to reach tree canopies, adult phase after ~10+ yr at 15-20 m; stems 50-66+ yr documented, one of 433 yr; legendary shade tolerance.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS and Wikipedia (Hedera helix: protandrous yellow-green flowers in globose umbels of 8-20, 3-5 cm across, late summer to late autumn, visited by >70 insect species, flies and wasps important late; berries 6-9 mm, black, 2-5 seeds, ripen Dec-May; bird-dispersed; somewhat poisonous). Fruit set, rot, crop estimated.
